payload.name: cepstral-peak-prominence-ratio
payload.scope: People made cepstral-peak-prominence-ratio to compare peak prominence against a reference baseline for normalized voicing decisions.

definition.body: Cepstral-peak-prominence-ratio is a human-made metric that quantifies the relative strength of a cepstral peak against a baseline prominence measure, used to normalize voicing decisions across varying signal conditions. Parameters: (1) the cepstral peak magnitude, (2) the baseline prominence estimate, (3) the quefrency search range. Persistence mechanism: documented in speech processing literature and implemented in pitch tracking libraries. e.g.: voicing decision normalization in the Voicebox MATLAB toolbox using prominence ratio; pitch analysis in Praat with prominence ratio metric; prominence ratio computation in the ESPS/waves+ speech analysis suite | not: cepstral-peak-to-average-ratio (ratio to global average, not baseline prominence); cepstral-peak-prominence (absolute prominence, not ratio) [formal: ratio prominentiae cepstralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

Law 7 which-came-first: the general cepstrum (Bogert, Healy, and Tukey 1963) is the original construct of the quefrency domain, and the complex cepstrum is a later variant that extends it to the full complex spectrum — the general predates the variant, and the variant is a specialization of the same framework. The note's closing clause ('relaxing the constraint to power spectrum only') is garbled — the complex variant uses the full complex spectrum, the 1963 original used the power spectrum — but the garble does not change the which-came-first result, which the note states and which holds from independent history. Type and direction both fit: the later to what it came from. Note: if the provisional complex-cepstrum entry falls, this edge voids with its stakes refunded.
